parse_units.normalized_content: Resolution Horizon
Experimental framework for measuring limits of invariant discovery from finite noisy observations under bounded computation.
Every finite observation process has a measurable resolution horizon k* beyond which additional structural depth models observational uncertainty rather than genuine invariants.
eta(k)=Delta L(k)/C_G(k), balancing structural compression value against symmetry ambiguity cost.
k*=argmax_k eta(k).
k*=f(N,sigma,E_cov,lambda_min(Gamma)).
Discovery: DeltaL rises/C_G falls; Horizon: eta peaks; Misresolution: DeltaL falls/C_G rises and uncertainty is fit as symmetry.
README identifies instrument.py as measurement core, experiment.py as regularization-bypass protocol, and test_suite.py as verification harness.
Scientific discovery is framed as a bounded measurement process asking what structure is recoverable under finite data, precision and computation.
Conceptual Theory: The Bounded Observer and Bounded Ontology
Structure is treated as emergent at the observer-system boundary under finite resources rather than intrinsic to the system in isolation.
Finite observers should model symmetries as resolution-dependent confidence regions rather than binary absolute classifications.
Observer constructs F_hat_{N,lambda_N} from localized trajectory samples and probes Lie_k(F_hat).
High-order differentiation amplifies noise; Var(D^k F_hat) is modeled as A_k sigma^2/N^{alpha_k}.
epsilon_k must widen with depth to accommodate derivative-estimation uncertainty.
Beyond k*, uncertainty inflation causes the estimated stabilizer to expand and admit distorted coordinate transformations as apparent symmetries.
Misresolution is distinguished from ordinary trajectory overfitting as overfitting the equivalence relation itself.
k* is interpreted as the critical point where marginal structural information gain matches marginal symmetry-uncertainty cost.
